james-letter.name: James
james-letter.role: Servant of God and the Lord Jesus Christ
james-letter.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
james-letter.importance: James greets the twelve tribes in the Dispersion. He tells them to ask God for wisdom and to be doers of the word. He warns against favoring the rich and against careless speech. He tells the sick to call for the elders.
james-letter.connections: He writes to the twelve tribes in the Dispersion. He calls them brothers.

jesus.name: Jesus Christ
jesus.role: Lord Jesus Christ, our glorious Lord
jesus.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jesus.importance: James names him in the greeting. James says not to hold the faith of our glorious Lord with partiality (chapter 2). A man in fine clothing gets a good seat. A poor man is told to stand. James calls that partiality.
jesus.connections: James calls himself a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ.

word.languageNote: This is the dictionary form of the name “Jesus.”

abraham.name: Abraham
abraham.role: Our father, called the friend of God
abraham.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abraham.importance: James says Abraham offered up his son Isaac on the altar. Faith worked with his works. James quotes Scripture that Abraham believed God, and it was counted as righteousness. Abraham was called the friend of God.
abraham.connections: James calls him our father. He ties his faith to his offering of Isaac.

isaac.name: Isaac
isaac.role: Abraham’s son, offered on the altar
isaac.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
isaac.importance: James names Isaac once. Abraham offered him up on the altar. James uses this act to show faith working with works.

rahab.name: Rahab
rahab.role: Woman called a prostitute, who received the messengers
rahab.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
rahab.importance: James calls her Rahab the prostitute. She received the messengers and sent them out another way. James says she was justified by works, as Abraham was.
rahab.connections: James places her after Abraham as a second example.

job.name: Job
job.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
job.importance: James tells the readers to be patient until the coming of the Lord. He calls those who endured blessed. He names Job’s perseverance. He says the Lord is full of compassion and mercy.
job.connections: James says his readers have heard of his perseverance. They have seen the Lord in the outcome.

elijah.name: Elijah
elijah.role: Prophet whose prayer stopped and brought rain
elijah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
elijah.importance: James says Elijah prayed earnestly that it might not rain. It did not rain for three years and six months. He prayed again, and the sky gave rain. James uses him to show that a righteous person’s prayer is powerful.
elijah.connections: James says he was a man with a nature like ours.
